correctness.rationale: For K_2 Cartesian K_n the neighbor field is exactly X-x_i+y_i and Y-y_i+x_i; strict-update and tie boundaries are treated. Even row sums give either row swapping at zero or uniform rows at nonzero sums, yielding an immediate-only two-cycle basin. Odd row sums permit nonuniform periodicity only at +/-1; the four-column type classification gives four primitive-two types and exactly two one-step predecessor types, with multinomial counts and all-state entry bounds. Distinct exhaustive direct state enumeration through n=8 (87,376 states) and weighted column-type checks through n=40 (135,746 types) match formulas including extrema. Finite tests are supporting checks, not the infinite proof.

evidence: Benjamini et al. give general eventual period <=2 and probability statements on unimodular and random graph families; they do not enumerate the deterministic two-clique matched graph's attracting sets.
Fountoulakis–Kang–Makai prove rapid consensus with high probability on binomial random graphs, not a universal labelled-state formula for a fixed family.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A general eventual-period bound or typical random-graph consensus theorem does not imply exact counts of one-step-preperiodic states on this deterministic regular graph. Existing period constraints are used as background only; the present proof independently establishes the all-state time cutoff.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Every compared earlier statement is insufficient to deduce the odd-case one-step tail mass 2n(n-1) binom(n-2,(n-3)/2) or the full basin formula. The new theorem classifies preperiodic, not just periodic, configurations; it also gives uniform entry-time cutoffs. The same graph under a different three-state local rule is a different dynamical system, not a covering result.

value.rationale: The target is the full basin of genuine oscillation, not merely the set of periodic configurations, in the natural fixed-graph family of two cliques joined by a perfect matching. The theorem classifies all one-step oscillation predecessors, shows a parity-selective creation of post-transient two-cycles, gives exact nonasymptotic populations and sharp time cutoffs, and exhibits polynomial-versus-exponential oscillation probability. These facts are not formal restatements of finite threshold-network period restrictions or static colorability, and quantify a structurally motivated dynamical question for arbitrarily large graphs.
